name: matrix-stack
title: Clock ticks with save, rotate and restore
summary: Twelve evenly spaced dial ticks drawn by one line inside a loop that translates to the centre, rotates by i·30° and restores the matrix each time.
prompt: Draw the twelve hour ticks of a clock dial by rotating the canvas in a loop.
teaches: Repeat a drawing around a centre by rotating the canvas inside a loop
Move the origin to the centre with translate so the shape is drawn at (0, −r)
Wrap each iteration's transform in save and restore so the rotations do not accumulate
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre
pitfalls: Without the restore, each iteration's translate and rotate stack on the previous ones: the origin moves another 100 dp every tick and all but the first leave the canvas
rotate turns about the current origin (0,0), so translate to the centre first; rotating before translating swings the centre itself around the top-left corner
`until` is exclusive: from 0 until 12 runs i = 0..11; with until 13 the 0° tick is drawn twice
Angles are degrees, clockwise; a tick at (0, -r) points to 12 o'clock

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())

snippets.note: loop i from 0 until 12 (12 is excluded)
rotate by the expression i * 30 (degrees) about the translated origin
one tick drawn straight up from the origin, at (0, -80) to (0, -62)
6 dp round-capped stroke for the ticks

check.describe: Twelve blue ticks evenly spaced 30° apart around a white centre dot. Resized, it scales to the shorter side and stays centred.
